standard_prerequisites.name: Relative finite presentation and its behaviour under a finite morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Morphisms, labels more-morphisms-definition-relatively-finitely-presented-sheaf (statement, proof line 4243), more-morphisms-lemma-relative-finite-presentation and more-morphisms-lemma-finite-morphism-relative-finite-presentation (proof lines 4266-4267)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the notion of being locally finitely presented relative to the base and shows that it is inherited from the pushforward along the closed immersion.

core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case and embed into an affine space: the question is local, so assume both schemes affine and choose a closed immersion of the source into an affine space over the base (proof lines 4247-4249).

Apply the finite presentation theorem upstairs: push the module forward along the closed immersion, note it is of finite type, and conclude that its flat locus is open and that its restriction there is of finite presentation (proof lines 4250-4256).

Descend to the source: the pushforward restricts to zero off the image and has the same stalks as the module at the points of the image, so its flat locus is the disjoint union of the image of the flat locus of the module and the complement of the image; hence the flat locus of the module is open, and the restriction of the module there is finitely presented relative to the base by the relative finite presentation statements (proof lines 4257-4267).
proof_roadmap: Go affine and embed into an affine space (proof lines 4247-4249).
Apply the finite presentation theorem to the pushforward (proof lines 4250-4256).
Read the flat locus of the module off the one upstairs and conclude relative finite presentation (proof lines 4257-4267).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves openness of the flat locus in the finite type case, with the additional conclusion that the restriction of the module to that locus is locally finitely presented relative to the base, by reduction to the finite presentation theorem (statement lines 4230-4245, tag 05IK-adjacent). The proof goes affine, embeds the source into an affine space over the base, applies the finite presentation theorem to the pushforward of the module, and then reads the flat locus of the module off the one computed upstairs using that the pushforward vanishes off the image and has the same stalks there, concluding relative finite presentation from the relative statements. The descent step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
